# Records and provenance

This page concerns representing operating models and their history, not the directory structure used to author this standard. No graph database, event-store technology or universal event log has been selected.

Candidate minimum information: identity; relevant revisions; typed relationships; scoped standing; attribution; source origin; decision history; occurrences; evidence linked to claims; assessment scope and limits. Preserve original evidence separately from current synthesis. Corrected interpretations should identify what they supersede without rewriting the source into the new interpretation.

## Retrieval questions the representation should support

- Why does this requirement exist, and whose need does it serve?
- What arrangement is expected to address it, and on which assumptions?
- What was assessed, under what conditions, with what evidence?
- What remains unknown or disputed?
- Who can change, perform, decide exceptions or accept the result?
- Which conclusions need reconsideration when a requirement, configuration or source changes?

The [EOM-06 working draft](../ontology/concepts/occurrences-and-state.md) distinguishes occurrences, states, observation acts and results, records, and evidence roles. It proposes separating subject time, observation time and recording time when relevant. It also proposes rules for missing capture, current-state claims, corrections and conflicting evidence. EOM-12 will determine the minimum representation; these distinctions do not make every item a required field or document kind.

[PROV-O](../../../source-locators.md#source-4ba3b6a5c02fa703) offers useful provenance distinctions. Its terminology is not a commitment to RDF/OWL, its full ontology, or any storage engine. The knowledge-graph/context-graph distinction raised by the owner remains a terminology question rather than a prerequisite for modeling history.

Open work: EOM-06 and EOM-12 in [the ledger](../../../source-locators.md#source-c43947fdcdae322a) cover history, minimum representation, retrieval and change propagation. Reuse small linked documents until explicit requirements justify richer machinery.

<a id="programmatic-consumption"></a>

## Programmatic consumption — proposal

Alongside human reading and agent-assisted interpretation, the human requested an ordinary programmatic consumer. The prospective `program.standard.validator` illustrates a bounded task: checking explicit record/reference rules. It does not establish an implemented consumer, production interface or selected storage format.

Where programmatic consumption is adopted, describe the relevant input/output contract and its revision, identifiable subjects and relations, allowed values or forms, and behavior when information is absent, unknown, incompatible or outside the supported contract. These are candidate interface concerns, not a requirement to duplicate every explanation in metadata or use JSON, RDF, a graph database or a particular validator.

Human/agent-facing prose and a program-consumable representation can be views of the same model. If both are maintained, their correspondence and changes need a defined basis; neither should silently introduce different meanings. Passing structural checks can establish only what the declared checks examine. It does not prove that a need is real, a contribution rationale is sound or a system serves its purpose.

The [self-application map](../../../source-locators.md#source-dbda9684ccaf624a) adds one proposed program-consumption need and one high-level requirement, with their conditional scope explicit. See [consumer-interface requirements](../ontology/concepts/requirement.md#requirements-from-consuming-systems--proposal) for the distinction between a useful dependency and circular justification.

## Document metadata convention

For how the authored documents themselves store identity, collection membership,
relationships and lifecycle metadata, use the shared [Document metadata standard](../../../source-locators.md#source-aef5f2b1d7a2f90d).
Its [Dublin Core baseline decision](../../../source-locators.md#source-7dfae5017d51720e)
does not settle the operating-model ontology or implement a lookup service.
